**Experiment 60: Quantization-aware wide from-scratch trunk** (category: `quantization`)

Core bet: 24 straight reverted rounds have exhausted decode/dispatcher/quantization-of-*location* families while only two ever touched the trunk's identity — and those two are the whole project's evidence that trunk capacity, not decode topology, is the real wall (domain-native contrastive from-scratch trunk got closest at 846m; a different pretrained family, ShuffleNetV2, did worse at 1552m). Every from-scratch trunk tried so far stored weights in FP32, capping its raw parameter count near what the banned champion trunk already has. This experiment trains a from-scratch conv trunk with genuine quantization-aware STE fake-quantization from step 1 (not post-hoc calibration), letting it be ~4-5x wider in raw parameters while still fitting the 4 MiB budget once INT8-packed via `onnxruntime.quantization.quantize_dynamic`. The champion's two-head brightness gate is also replaced by continuous FiLM conditioning (single field head, freeing more byte budget). Every stage — trunk, lighting conditioning, layout summary, field, rotation ensemble, decode wiring, confidence, quantization export, sampler, optimizer, loss — is rebuilt around this one mechanism, satisfying this round's full-pivot bar without touching the banned `mobilenet_v3_small`/`mnv3s_features8.pt` identifiers.

The implementation brief gives file-level instructions for `model/model.py` (QATConv2d/QATLinear wrappers, trunk shape, FiLM, single field head, weight-freeze-before-export) and `model/train.py` (single-LR optimizer, freeze step, dynamic INT8 export packing), while explicitly leaving the training-data sampler and schedule untouched to keep this a one-variable test. Design stage is done — the implementation agent picks this up next.
